translations.literal: The order and disorder of a whole state rest on the ruler and chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a realm is well governed or in chaos, the ruler and his chief minister bear responsibility.

translations.literal: The order and disorder of a region rest on the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder in a province fall to its frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 清制：疆帥之重，幾埒宰輔。

translations.literal: Under Qing institutions, the weight of frontier commanders nearly equaled that of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing system, frontier governors-general wielded authority almost on a par with grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 選材特愼，部院莫儗，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: Selection of personnel was especially careful; no board or court could be compared—presumably for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Men were chosen with exceptional care, unmatched among the boards and courts—and for good reason.

sentences.zh: 開國而後，戡藩拓邊，率資其用。

translations.literal: After the founding of the state, pacifying feudatories and expanding the frontier largely relied on their employment.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding onward, suppressing feudatories and pushing the frontier forward depended chiefly on them.

sentences.zh: 同治中興，光緒還都，皆非疆帥無與成功。

translations.literal: The Tongzhi Restoration and the Guangxu return to the capital—none could succeed without frontier commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the Tongzhi revival nor the Guangxu restoration could have succeeded without these frontier governors.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，始削其權，則不國矣。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign changed its era name, their powers were first reduced—then it was no longer a state.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Xuantong reign began were their powers curtailed—and with that the dynasty was lost.

sentences.zh: 唐之方鎭，元之行省，史不表人，識者病之。

translations.literal: Tang regional commands and Yuan branch secretariats—the histories did not tabulate persons; the discerning found this fault.
translations.idiomatic: Tang military governors and Yuan provincial administrations went untabulated in the histories, a lapse thoughtful readers deplored.

sentences.zh: 今表疆臣，先列督撫，附以河漕。

translations.literal: Now this table lists frontier officials, first setting out governors-general and governors, with river and grain transport appended.
translations.idiomatic: This table presents frontier officials, listing governors-general and governors first, with river and grain transport posts appended.

sentences.zh: 東三省外，北盡蒙疆，西極回藏，將軍、都統、參贊、辦事大臣有專地者，皆如疆帥，今並著焉。

translations.literal: Beyond the three eastern provinces, north to the Mongol frontier, west to Xinjiang and Tibet, generals, commandants, deputy commissioners, and resident ministers holding exclusive territories—all like frontier commanders—are now included together.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the three Northeast provinces, from the northern Mongol borderlands to Xinjiang and Tibet in the west, territorial posts such as generals, commandants, deputy commissioners, and resident ministers with exclusive jurisdictions—all ranking as frontier governors—are included here as well.
